brand: false
execute:
  freeze: false
format:

    title: "Chesterfield County needs affordable homes for the people who serve it"
    toc: false
  typst:
    papersize: us-letter
    margin:
      x: 0.55in
      y: 0.15in
    fontsize: 7.5pt
    mainfont: Lato
    font-paths: ["fonts"]
    toc: false
    fig-format: png
    fig-dpi: 200

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

source("_common.R")

# BHC brand: Lato (Brand Identity Guide typefaces), registered for ggplot2 text.
systemfonts::register_font(
  "BHC Lato",
  plain = "fonts/Lato-Regular.ttf", bold = "fonts/Lato-Bold.ttf",
  italic = "fonts/Lato-Italic.ttf", bolditalic = "fonts/Lato-Bold.ttf"
)
systemfonts::register_font("BHC Lato Black", plain = "fonts/Lato-Black.ttf")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "ragg_png")

g <- rva_guide # BHC Brand Identity Guide palette
html <- knitr::is_html_output()

# Pages read_rds() only.
op <- read_rds("data/chesterfield_onepager.rds") # r/chesterfield_afford.R
afford <- op$afford
ctx <- op$ctx
cc <- read_rds("data/chesterfield_context.rds") # r/chesterfield_context.R
bur_all <- read_rds("data/acs_burden.rds") |> filter(geoid == "51041")
bur <- bur_all |> filter(year == 2024)
ten <- read_rds("data/acs_market.rds")$tenure |> filter(geoid == "51041", tenure != "Total")
demo <- read_rds("data/acs_demographics.rds")
pep <- read_rds("data/pep_migration.rds")$annual |> filter(geoid == "51041")
pums <- read_rds("data/pums_profiles.rds")

usd <- scales::label_dollar(accuracy = 1)
usd0 <- \(x) usd(round(x))
pct <- scales::label_percent(accuracy = 1)
num <- scales::label_comma()

## ---- Pay (one row per role: latest confirmed figure, proposed beside it) ----
cur <- afford |>
  arrange(role, factor(status, c("current", "stale", "proposed"))) |>
  slice(1, .by = role)
prop <- afford |>
  filter(status == "proposed") |>
  select(role, proposed_pay = annual_pay)
roles <- cur |>
  left_join(prop, by = "role") |>
  mutate(proposed_pay = if_else(status == "proposed", NA_real_, proposed_pay)) |>
  arrange(desc(annual_pay))

tag_for <- \(status, source_date, basis) paste0(
  case_match(status,
    "proposed" ~ " (proposed)",
    "stale" ~ paste0(" (", format(source_date, "%b %Y"), " posting)"),
    .default = ""
  ),
  if_else(basis == "hourly", " (hourly x 2,080 hrs)", "")
)
roles <- roles |> mutate(role_label = paste0(role, tag_for(status, source_date, basis)))
police <- afford |> filter(role == "Police officer") |> slice(1)
two_ff <- 2 * police$annual_pay

## ---- Cost burden (ACS 2020-2024, B25070 / B25091) ----
bt <- bur |>
  filter(burden != "Not computed") |>
  mutate(share = estimate / sum(estimate), .by = tenure)
n_burdened <- bt |> filter(burden != "Not cost-burdened") |> pull(estimate) |> sum()
share_burdened <- n_burdened / sum(bt$estimate)
b_share <- \(ten) bt |> filter(tenure == ten, burden != "Not cost-burdened") |> pull(share) |> sum()
renter_b <- b_share("Renter")
owner_b <- b_share("Owner")

## ---- Renters (ACS B25003 and B25070, 2014 / 2019 / 2024) ----
renters <- ten |> filter(tenure == "Renter") |> select(year, n = estimate)
rn <- \(y) renters$n[renters$year == y]
renter_growth <- rn(2024) / rn(2014) - 1
rb <- bur_all |>
  filter(tenure == "Renter", burden %in% c("Cost-burdened", "Severely cost-burdened")) |>
  mutate(burden = factor(burden, c("Severely cost-burdened", "Cost-burdened"), c("50%+ of income", "30-49% of income")))
rb_tot <- rb |> summarise(n = sum(estimate), .by = year)
rbn <- \(y) rb_tot$n[rb_tot$year == y]
rb_growth <- rbn(2024) / rbn(2014) - 1

## ---- Income distribution (PUMS vs HUD FY2026 limits) ----
ami_lv <- c("30% AMI or less", "31-50% AMI", "51-80% AMI", "81-120% AMI", "Above 120% AMI")
ami <- pums$dist5 |>
  filter(geo == "Chesterfield County", tenure == "All households", unit == "Households", measure == "share") |>
  transmute(band = factor(as.character(band), ami_lv), share = est) |>
  arrange(band)
le80 <- pums$le80 |>
  filter(geo == "Chesterfield County", unit == "Households", tenure == "All households") |> pull(est)
le80_renter <- pums$le80 |>
  filter(geo == "Chesterfield County", unit == "Households", tenure == "Renter") |> pull(est)

## ---- Seniors (ACS B25007, B25072, B25093, B01001) ----
sr_hh <- cc$hh_age |>
  summarise(n = sum(estimate), .by = c(year, age)) |>
  filter(age == "65 and over")
sr_hh14 <- sr_hh$n[sr_hh$year == 2014]
sr_hh24 <- sr_hh$n[sr_hh$year == 2024]
sr_pop <- demo$age_sex |>
  filter(geoid == "51041", age_group == "65 and over") |>
  summarise(n = sum(estimate), .by = year)
sr_burden <- cc$burden_age |>
  summarise(share = sum(estimate[burdened]) / sum(estimate), .by = c(tenure, age)) |>
  mutate(
    tenure = factor(tenure, c("Renter", "Owner"), c("Renters", "Owners")),
    age = factor(age, c("65 and over", "Under 65"), c("Householder 65+", "Under 65"))
  )
sr_get <- \(ten, a) sr_burden |> filter(tenure == ten, age == a) |> pull(share)

## ---- Household size and bedrooms (ACS B25009, B25042) ----
size24 <- cc$hh_size |>
  filter(year == 2024) |>
  summarise(n = sum(estimate), .by = size) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n))
bed24 <- cc$bedrooms |>
  filter(year == 2024) |>
  summarise(n = sum(estimate), .by = bedrooms) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n))
small_hh <- sum(size24$share[size24$size != "3+ people"])
small_homes <- sum(bed24$share[bed24$bedrooms != "3+ bedrooms"])

## ---- Growth, 2014 to 2024 (index, 2014 = 100) ----
hh_tot <- cc$hh_size |> summarise(v = sum(estimate), .by = year)
alone <- demo$household_type |>
  filter(geoid == "51041", household_type == "Living alone") |>
  select(year, v = estimate)
pop_acs <- demo$population |> filter(geoid == "51041") |> select(year, v = estimate)
growth <- bind_rows(
  mutate(sr_hh |> select(year, v = n), series = "Householders 65+"),
  mutate(hh_tot, series = "All households"),
  mutate(alone, series = "People living alone"),
  mutate(pop_acs, series = "Population")
) |>
  mutate(index = 100 * v / v[year == 2014], .by = series)
gr <- \(s) growth |> filter(series == s, year == 2024) |> pull(index) / 100 - 1
pop10 <- pep$pop[pep$year == 2010]
pop25 <- pep$pop[pep$year == 2025]
pop_growth <- pop25 / pop10 - 1

# Chart titles and tiles state these claims; stop the render if the data stops supporting them.
stopifnot(
  "claim: every role is short of the median rent" = all(roles$rent_gap < 0),
  "claim: two police incomes clear the median-home income" = two_ff > ctx$income_for_home,
  "claim: every salary is below 80% AMI (1 person)" = all(roles$annual_pay < ctx$ami80_1p),
  "claim: renters more burdened than owners" = renter_b > owner_b,
  "claim: renter households grew" = rn(2024) > rn(2019) && rn(2019) > rn(2014),
  "claim: burdened renters grew faster than renters" = rb_growth > renter_growth,
  "claim: about one in three households is at or below 80% AMI" = between(le80, 0.30, 0.37),
  "claim: senior renters more burdened than younger renters" =
    sr_get("Renters", "Householder 65+") > sr_get("Renters", "Under 65"),
  "claim: small households outnumber small homes" = small_hh > small_homes + 0.2,
  "claim: households outgrew population" = gr("All households") > gr("Population"),
  "claim: senior households grew fastest" =
    gr("Householders 65+") > max(gr("All households"), gr("People living alone"), gr("Population"))
)
asm <- ctx$assumptions

## ---- Output helpers: one markup for HTML, another for Typst ----
typ_esc <- \(x) gsub("([\\\\$#*_@<>`~\\[\\]])", "\\\\\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
raw_typst <- \(x) cat("```{=typst}\n", x, "\n```\n", sep = "")
tile_values <- c(
  num(n_burdened), paste0("+", pct(renter_growth)), paste0("+", pct(rb_growth)), pct(le80)
)
tile_labels <- c(
  paste0("households pay 30%+ of income on housing (", pct(share_burdened), " of the county)"),
  paste0("renter households since 2014, from ", num(rn(2014)), " to ", num(rn(2024))),
  paste0("cost-burdened renter households since 2014, from ", num(rbn(2014)), " to ", num(rbn(2024))),
  "of households earn 80% of area median income or less"
)

# Section heading: Markdown H2 in HTML, a teal title over an orange rule in Typst
# (raw Typst is block-scoped, so a heading show rule cannot be set globally).
h2 <- function(title) {
  if (html) {
    cat("\n## ", title, "\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    raw_typst(paste0(
      "#block(above: 9pt, below: 0pt, breakable: false)[#text(size: 10.5pt, weight: 900, fill: rgb(\"#00617F\"))[",
      typ_esc(title), "]#v(-3pt)#line(length: 100%, stroke: 1.4pt + rgb(\"#E86C1F\"))]
"
    ))
  }
}

# ggplot theme in BHC type and colors
theme_bhc <- function(base_size = 7) {
  theme_rva(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "BHC Lato", color = g[["ink"]]),
      plot.title = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        family = "BHC Lato Black", size = rel(1.2), color = g[["teal"]],
        width = unit(1, "npc"), margin = margin(b = 2), lineheight = 1.05
      ),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_textbox_simple(
        size = rel(0.95), color = "#555555", width = unit(1, "npc"), margin = margin(b = 4)
      ),
      axis.text = element_text(color = g[["ink"]]),
      axis.line.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      # Each chart is a "card": white with a thin cream border, so side-by-side charts read as separate.
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = g[["cream"]], linewidth = 0.9),
      plot.margin = margin(5, 8, 4, 6),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
}

# Print several ggplots side by side in one device (one figure, one alt text).
row_of <- function(plots, widths = rep(1, length(plots))) {
  grid::grid.newpage()
  n <- length(plots)
  # Fixed 7pt gutters between the chart cards.
  w <- grid::unit.c(
    grid::unit(widths[1], "null"),
    do.call(grid::unit.c, lapply(seq_len(n)[-1], \(i) grid::unit.c(grid::unit(7, "pt"), grid::unit(widths[i], "null"))))
  )
  grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = grid::grid.layout(1, 2 * n - 1, widths = w)))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    print(plots[[i]], vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.col = 2 * i - 1))
  }
  invisible()
}
```

```{r}
#| output: asis
#| echo: false
```
```{r}
h2("Public-service starting pay falls short of the median rent")
```

```{r}
#| label: pay-chart
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.225
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bars of starting pay for seven Chesterfield public-service roles, from about $37,000 for instructional assistants to $60,147 for police officers and firefighters. Each role's label states the rent and home price one income affords. A vertical line near $65,000 marks the income needed for the median rent and a dashed line near $117,000 the income needed for the median home; every bar falls short of both. Diamonds mark proposed FY27 pay where it differs."

plot_df <- roles |>
  mutate(
    lab = paste0(
      role_label, "
rent ", usd0(max_rent), " · home ", usd0(max_price)
    ),
    lab = fct_reorder(lab, annual_pay)
  )

ggplot(plot_df, aes(annual_pay, lab)) +
  geom_col(fill = g[["orange"]], width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(aes(label = usd0(annual_pay)), hjust = 1.1, size = 2.5, color = g[["ink"]], fontface = "bold", family = "BHC Lato") +
  geom_point(
    data = filter(plot_df, !is.na(proposed_pay)), aes(proposed_pay),
    shape = 23, size = 2.4, fill = g[["amber"]], color = g[["ink"]], stroke = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ctx$income_for_rent, color = g[["teal"]], linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = ctx$income_for_home, color = g[["teal"]], linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = ctx$income_for_rent + 1500, y = 7, hjust = 0, size = 2.5, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold",
           color = g[["teal"]], label = paste0("Median rent needs\n",usd0(ctx$income_for_rent))) +
  annotate("text", x = ctx$income_for_home - 1500, y = 7, hjust = 1, size = 2.5, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold",
           color = g[["teal"]], label = paste0("Median home needs\n",usd0(ctx$income_for_home))) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-3, suffix = "k"), breaks = seq(0, 125000, 25000),
    limits = c(0, 132000), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Every starting salary falls short of both lines",
    subtitle = "Annual starting pay, one earner, 2026. Diamonds mark proposed FY27 pay; labels show the most rent and home price that pay affords."
  ) +
  theme_bhc() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(lineheight = 1.0, face = "plain"),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = rva_ink[["gridline"]])
  )
```

- Starting pay for seven county and school roles is `{r} usd0(min(roles$annual_pay))` to `{r} usd0(max(roles$annual_pay))`; every role is short of the median rent of `{r} usd0(ctx$median_rent)` by `{r} usd0(-max(roles$rent_gap))` to `{r} usd0(-min(roles$rent_gap))` a month.
- The best starting salary affords a home near `{r} usd0(max(roles$max_price))`, about half the median value of `{r} usd0(ctx$median_value)`; two police incomes (`{r} usd0(two_ff)`) are just enough.

```{r}
#| output: asis

h2("More renters, and more of them are stretched thin")
```

```{r}
#| label: renter-panels
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.14
#| fig-alt: "Two panels. Left: bars of Chesterfield renter households in 2014, 2019 and 2024, rising from about 27,000 to about 33,000. Right: stacked bars of cost-burdened renter households for the same years, split into those paying 30 to 49 percent and 50 percent or more of income, rising from about 12,000 to about 16,000."

ra <- renters |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), n)) +
  geom_col(fill = g[["orange"]], width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = num(n)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]]) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Renter households are up ", pct(renter_growth), " since 2014"),
    subtitle = "Occupied rental homes, ACS 5-year ending in the year shown"
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(axis.line.x = element_line(color = rva_ink[["baseline"]]), axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"))

rb_lab <- rb_tot |> mutate(lab = num(n))
rbp <- rb |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(year), estimate, fill = burden)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = num(estimate)), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.4, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]]) +
  geom_text(data = rb_lab, aes(y = n, label = lab, fill = NULL), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.6, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("30-49% of income" = g[["amber"]], "50%+ of income" = g[["orange"]])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
  labs(
    title = paste0("Cost-burdened renter households are up ", pct(rb_growth)),
    subtitle = "Paying 30%+ of income on rent: 30-49% (amber), 50%+ (orange)"
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(axis.line.x = element_line(color = rva_ink[["baseline"]]), axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"))

row_of(list(ra, rbp))
```

- Renter households grew by `{r} num(rn(2024) - rn(2014))` in ten years, and cost-burdened renters grew faster; `{r} pct(le80_renter)` of renters earn 80% of area median income or less.

```{r}
h2("Housing cost burden is widespread, and heaviest for renters and seniors")
```

```{r}
#| label: need-panels
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.19
#| fig-alt: "Three panels. Left: stacked bars of cost-burdened share of Chesterfield renters (about half) and owners (about one in five). Middle: share of households by income band relative to area median income; about one in three is at or below 80 percent. Right: share of households that are cost-burdened by tenure, for householders 65 and over versus under 65; senior renters are the most burdened at about two in three."

burden_lab <- c("Not cost-burdened" = "Under 30% of income", "Cost-burdened" = "30-49%", "Severely cost-burdened" = "50%+")
pa <- bt |>
  mutate(
    tenure = factor(tenure, c("Owner", "Renter"), c("Owners", "Renters")),
    burden = factor(burden, c("Not cost-burdened", "Cost-burdened", "Severely cost-burdened"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(share, tenure, fill = fct_rev(burden))) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share)), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 2.5, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Not cost-burdened" = g[["sky"]], "Cost-burdened" = g[["amber"]], "Severely cost-burdened" = g[["orange"]]),
    labels = burden_lab, breaks = names(burden_lab)
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 3, title = NULL, reverse = FALSE, keywidth = 0.6, keyheight = 0.6)) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(pct(renter_b), " of renters and ", pct(owner_b), " of owners are cost-burdened"),
    subtitle = "Share of households by housing cost as a share of income, 2020-2024"
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 6), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
                      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

pb <- ami |>
  mutate(
    low = band %in% ami_lv[1:3],
    lab = factor(band, ami_lv, c("30% or less", "31-50%", "51-80%", "81-120%", "Over 120%"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(lab, share, fill = low)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share)), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.5, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = g[["orange"]], `FALSE` = g[["sky"]])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "One in three households earns 80% of area median income or less",
    subtitle = paste0("Share of households by income as a share of AMI. Renters: ", pct(le80_renter), " at or below 80%.")
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), axis.line.x = element_line(color = rva_ink[["baseline"]]))

pc <- sr_burden |>
  ggplot(aes(tenure, share, fill = age)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), vjust = -0.4, size = 2.5, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]]) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Householder 65+" = g[["teal"]], "Under 65" = g[["sky"]])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.32))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2, title = NULL, keywidth = 0.6, keyheight = 0.6)) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(pct(sr_get("Renters", "Householder 65+")), " of senior renters are cost-burdened"),
    subtitle = paste0("Paying 30%+ of income. 65+ households: ", num(sr_hh14), " (2014) to ", num(sr_hh24), " (2024)")
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 6), legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
                      axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"), axis.line.x = element_line(color = rva_ink[["baseline"]]))

row_of(list(pa, pb, pc))
```


```{r}
#| label: size-panels
#| fig-width: 7.4
#| fig-asp: 0.16
#| fig-alt: "Two panels. Left: two stacked bars comparing households by size with occupied homes by bedrooms in Chesterfield; most households have one or two people while most homes have three or more bedrooms. Right: lines showing growth since 2014 for householders 65 and over, all households, people living alone and population; senior households grew fastest."

seg_cols <- c("1" = g[["orange"]], "2" = g[["amber"]], "3" = g[["sky"]])
pd <- bind_rows(
  size24 |> transmute(bar = "Households\n(people)", seg = recode_values(size, "1 person" ~ "1", "2 people" ~ "2", "3+ people" ~ "3"),
                      name = recode_values(size, "1 person" ~ "1", "2 people" ~ "2", "3+ people" ~ "3+"), share),
  bed24 |> transmute(bar = "Occupied homes\n(bedrooms)", seg = recode_values(bedrooms, "0-1 bedroom" ~ "1", "2 bedrooms" ~ "2", "3+ bedrooms" ~ "3"),
                     name = recode_values(bedrooms, "0-1 bedroom" ~ "0-1", "2 bedrooms" ~ "2", "3+ bedrooms" ~ "3+"), share)
) |>
  mutate(bar = factor(bar, c("Occupied homes\n(bedrooms)", "Households\n(people)")))
pd_plot <- ggplot(pd, aes(share, bar, fill = seg)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(name, "\n", pct(share))), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = FALSE),
            size = 2.3, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", color = g[["ink"]], lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = seg_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(
    title = paste0(pct(small_hh), " of households have one or two people; only ", pct(small_homes), " of homes have two or fewer bedrooms"),
    subtitle = "Chesterfield, 2020-2024. Orange and amber are the smaller sizes."
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"))

gl <- growth |>
  mutate(series = factor(series, c("Householders 65+", "All households", "People living alone", "Population")))
lab_df <- gl |> filter(year == 2024) |> mutate(lab = paste0(series, " +", round(index - 100), "%")) |> arrange(index)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(lab_df))[-1]) lab_df$index[i] <- max(lab_df$index[i], lab_df$index[i - 1] + 16) # keep end labels apart
pe_plot <- ggplot(gl, aes(year, index, color = series, group = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  geom_text(data = lab_df, aes(label = lab), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.35, size = 2.4, family = "BHC Lato", fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Householders 65+" = g[["teal"]], "All households" = g[["orange"]],
                                "People living alone" = "#8a8a8a", "Population" = "#c9a96a")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2014, 2019, 2024), limits = c(2013.6, 2032.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(95, 182)) +
  labs(
    title = "Senior households and household count are growing faster than population",
    subtitle = "Index, 2014 = 100 (2010-14, 2015-19, 2020-24 ACS)"
  ) +
  theme_bhc() + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = rva_ink[["gridline"]]),
                      axis.line.x = element_line(color = rva_ink[["baseline"]]))

row_of(list(pd_plot, pe_plot), widths = c(1.05, 0.95))
```

```{r}
notes <- paste0(
  "One earner, starting pay. Affordable rent is 30% of gross income; cost burden means 30% or more of income goes to housing. ",
  "Home price assumes a ", scales::percent(asm$rate, accuracy = 0.01), " 30-year mortgage (Freddie Mac, week of ", format(asm$rate_date, "%b %d, %Y"),
  "), ", scales::percent(asm$down_pct, accuracy = 1), " down, the county's proposed FY2027 real estate tax rate (", sprintf("$%.2f", asm$tax_rate * 100),
  " per $100), insurance at ", scales::percent(asm$ins_rate, accuracy = 0.01), " of price and mortgage insurance at ", scales::percent(asm$pmi_rate, accuracy = 0.1),
  " of the loan (the last two are our assumptions). Hourly pay is annualized at 2,080 hours; school-year workers earn less. ",
  "Teacher and bus driver pay is the FY26 scale; FY27 pay is proposed, not confirmed adopted. Deputy sheriff pay is from a January 2026 posting; the 911 officer figure is the class-specification minimum. ",
  "AMI is HUD's FY2026 area median income for the Richmond area, adjusted for household size. Median rent and home value are 2020-2024 ACS."
)
if (html) {
  cat('::: {.callout-note}\n## How to read these figures\n', notes, '\n:::\n\n', sep = "")
  cat(chesterfield_pay_cap(), "\n")
} else {
  raw_typst(paste0(
    "#v(3pt)\n#block(width: 100%, fill: rgb(\"#FEF3CF\"), inset: 4pt)[#set text(size: 5.4pt)\n#strong[How to read these figures.] ", typ_esc(notes), "]\n"
  ))
  cat("\n```{=typst}\n#set text(size: 5.5pt)\n```\n\n")
  cat(chesterfield_pay_cap(), "\n")
}
```
